title: Port Matilda man charged with threatening President-elect Donald J. Trump
text:
John C. Gurganus Acting United States Attorney for the Middle District of Pennsylvania | Department of Justice
John C. Gurganus Acting United States Attorney for the Middle District of Pennsylvania | Department of Justice
Jacob Buckley, 22, of Port Matilda in Centre County, Pennsylvania, has been charged with threatening Donald J. Trump while he was President-elect. The announcement was made by the United States Attorney’s Office for the Middle District of Pennsylvania.
According to Acting United States Attorney John Gurganus, Buckley is accused of using a TikTok account under the name “Jacob_buckley” to post several threatening messages on January 16, 2025. The posts included: “I hate MAGA republicans bro on god I’ll kill all of them”; “I’m going to kill Trump”; and, “Bro we going into a literal oligarchy in 4 days and im going to kill Trump.”
The investigation was conducted by the United States Secret Service. Assistant United States Attorney K. Wesley Mishoe is prosecuting the case.
If convicted, Buckley could face up to five years in prison, supervised release after imprisonment, a fine, and a special assessment. Sentencing would follow federal guidelines and statutes.
It was noted that criminal informations are only allegations and all individuals charged are presumed innocent unless found guilty in court.
